gen-dafont-electroharmonix-gf-lexend-gig: Electroharmonix breaks every word into lonely, separate letters. Its open-handed curves grab attention, while Lexend Giga, with generous tracking and flat single-weight linework, keeps each word easy to follow.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono stands its letters like pins in a wide board, with a compact skyline. Cascadia Mono's rounded-wire strokes are the standout, a hush beside the fast, spread-out letters of Ethnocentric.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega flows like a single-nib line, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals. But Ethnocentric is the one for impact, fast and aggressive, while the body font handles the steady work of being read.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta reads wide and full, its curves never thinning and its x-height towering over tight ascenders. And Ethnocentric shoves in fast and aggressive, its spaced-out letters giving the sans below a loud introduction.
gen-dafont-galaxy-gf-cascadia-code: Cosmic and loose, with lines that never change width. Galaxy carries that loose, starry spacing up top, while Cascadia Code draws a wire-like monoline skeleton with smooth bends below.
gen-dafont-galaxy-gf-lexend-exa: Galaxy drifts across the line with loose, uninterrupted strokes. Lexend Exa grounds it with broad, distinct curves, stubby ascenders and a big x-height, giving the layout a loose sky above a sturdy floor.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-montserrat-alternat: Friendly and funky, with a c nearly squeezed shut. Groovy is the closed one here, while Montserrat Alternates swings its c wide as a bent paperclip, with chalk-board lowercase crowding the capital line.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-lexend-exa: Heavy, blunt and spaced like beads on a rod, each letter alone. Impact Label hits hardest as the commanding heading, while Lexend Exa does its best work in stubby, uniform-thickness text.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-lexend-giga: Heavy letters, each one standing alone like a bead. Impact Label is built to command with its pincer-like c, while Lexend Giga does its best work through flat, single-weight linework and generous tracking.
